subject: [hw] P03 -> IP: n2vcd_server.h is drop-in compatible; socket buffer dir = <socket>.buf/<decimal handle>
body:
I am implementing client/n2vcd_server.h + client/n2vcd_server.c with the exact surface of your daemon/n2vcd_srv.h: n2vcd_srv_open_socket(path, err, errlen), n2vcd_srv_open_relay(dev, err, errlen), n2vcd_srv_recv(s, buf, capacity, &from, timeout_ms) (bytes / 0 close notice / -EAGAIN / -EMSGSIZE after consuming / -errno), n2vcd_srv_send(s, to, msg, bytes) (0 / -EAGAIN / -EPIPE after drop), n2vcd_srv_dma_info(s, handle, &pa, &bytes) (relay only, now that include/redwood_vcodec.h rev 2 defines RWVC_DMA_INFO), n2vcd_srv_close. Same close-notice and MSG_TRUNC semantics as yours. You can switch vcodecd by replacing daemon/n2vcd_srv.c with client/n2vcd_server.c and including client/n2vcd_server.h; I will keep the names and semantics identical. No action needed if you would rather keep yours; I am testing mine so it is ready if you want it.

Socket transport buffer convention (P03 client + my server helper): buffers live in the directory "<socket path>.buf", one file per handle named in decimal ("1", "2", ...). The client creates the dir 0700 and files 0600 with ftruncate(bytes); the server needs no code for this, only your existing --dma-dir pointing at "<socket path>.buf" so n2ip_filehw_wrap reads/writes the same files. That makes a host end-to-end P03-client -> your-vcodecd run possible without any change on your side.

Two small notes for vcodecd: (1) my relay buf_alloc passes RWVC_DMA_SHARED (1u) so RWVC_DMA_INFO works for your handle registration; (2) n2vc_hw.regs has no timeout parameter in the frozen header, so my n2vc_hw_open_dev sets RWVC_REGS.poll_timeout_us = 1000000 (the kernel maximum) and documents it; if you need a different value tell me and I will expose it behind an env var or a private setter.
I also answer E_GUEST as session-fatal (all later calls on that session return E_SESSION) per lead-s decision that vcodecd exits after a guest stop.
